stemMd: A solution contains 0.40 mol sodium chloride in 2.0 L. Assuming complete dissociation, what is the sodium-ion concentration?
explanationMd: Each formula unit of NaCl gives one sodium ion, so sodium amount is 0.40 mol. Dividing by 2.0 L gives 0.20 mol/L. Chloride has the same individual concentration; adding both would give total ion concentration, a different quantity.

distractorRationale.b: This uses moles as if they were already concentration.
distractorRationale.d: This multiplies by volume rather than dividing.
distractorRationale.e: This incorrectly divides again because the salt gives two ion types.
distractorRationale.c: This does not follow the amount-to-volume ratio.
